Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Money, work & business · Town, shops & places

beggar noun

also beggars, beg, begging, beg for money

classical

Plaut. Trin. 339: dē mendīcō male merētur quī eī dat quod edit aut bibat
Cic. Fin. 5.84: mendīcus esse beātus nēmō potest (Lewis & Short)

mendīcus, mendīcī m.

noun, second declension

a beggar

Properly an adjective, needy, beggarly; as a noun, a beggar (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • mendīcō, mendīcāre, mendīcāvī, mendīcātum — beg, live by begging

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Plaut. Capt. 323: mendīcantem vīvere, to live by begging; Suet. Aug. 91.2: stipem … ēmendīcābat ā populō, he begged alms from the people

    Also deponent, mendīcor (Plaut.); to beg something from someone, ēmendīcāre.

Examples

  • animadvertī pauperem mendīcum, jam, crēdō, saturum, jocantem atque laetantem

    I noticed a poor beggar, already full, I suppose, joking and cheerfulAug. Conf. 6.6.9

  • aequō mendīcus atque ille opulentissimus cēnsētur cēnsū ad Acheruntem mortuos

    among the dead by Acheron the beggar and the richest man are rated at the same worthPlaut. Trin. 493–494

See also alms, poor, poverty, rich.

SourcesLewis & Short: mendicus · Lewis & Short: mendico
